for_you_if: you want large scale multiplayer action despite technical hurdles
you look past missing game modes

you will not adjust bios settings or enable secure boot
you expect a traditional server browser

claims.claim: Matchmaking places low-level players into lobbies with much higher-level opponents, creating a lack of balance.

citations.review_text:
Will games like this ever have actual matchmaking balance?  Why do I join a match as a level 1 player, get matched with level 100-150 players on my team, and then have to fight level 200 no-life sweats who have apparently been grinding Battlefield since they were still in their mother's womb?

Did the developers seriously think that making the game extremely cinematic would automatically make it good? Did they think throwing a bunch of marketing buІІshіt at people would be enough to sell it? Well, apparently it was. A lot of people bought into it. That is what good advertising can do. Yeah, yeah, keep releasing the same game over and over again, improve the graphics, add a few things, remove a few others, and call it a new Battlefield. And charging €70 for the game while also stuffing a Battle Pass into it is hilarious. Sure, it is currently discounted to around €35, but that does not really change the point.

When are games going to stop being designed by greedy executives whose main goal is squeezing as much money as possible out of players, and start being made by people who actually play games? Modders are a perfect example. Half the time they feel like gods compared to actual paid developers. They fix things, add features people actually want, and somehow manage to understand the game better without being paid a salary for it. And the funniest part is that many of them either survive entirely on donations or do it for free, yet somehow manage to do their work several times better and with more care than actual paid developers. Lol.

Battlefield 6 was the only Battlefield game I ever had on my wishlist. Luckily, I got the chance to try it for free before buying it. And thanks to that, I now know that even if Battlefield 7, 8, or 9 eventually comes out, I will not even bother adding them to my wishlist.

So with this kind of attitude, Battlefield 6 can go fхсk itself. And Electronic Arts can go with it.

claims.claim: Progression and unlocking weapon attachments require an excessively long grind.

citations.review_text:
My head hurts. Is there a doctor in the house?
A typical Battlefield 6 match consists of frustrations related to the following:


- Disappointingly small maps compared to other Battlefield titles.
- Player counts that are way too high for said undersized maps.
- We're talking about some abysmal map design here. Like, who in their right mind thought some of these layouts were a good idea?
- Extremely fast time-to-kill. It's literally Adderall mode—just run and gun.
- Too few weapons.
- Progression is painfully slow.
- Air vehicles are nearly impossible to use. The controls are awful.
- Graphics look like they're from older games that came out 13 years ago, running in raster, yet somehow the game runs significantly worse—even with upscaling technology.
- The visual filters are completely off-theme. Everything is way too vibrant and colorful.
- Battle pass system.
- Paid in-game currency.
- Expensive Game Price.

Everyone is constantly chasing red dots on the map. Because the maps are so small and the player counts are so high, almost every enemy encounter turns into a fight against at least 3–4 people. You down one guy? Well, get ready to fight his entire squad as they come charging up behind him.
And what's that? You want to equip a suppressor so you're not immediately visible on the map when firing? Get ready to spend 3–8 hours of absolute hell grinding one suppressor per gun.

Guys what happend.

Hot garbage weapon xp farming simulator. Oh what's that? You want all the attachments on a few of the guns? That'll be hundreds of hours of gameplay. What's what?? You work and have a family?? You only game for a few hours a night? Tough break kiddo, you're going to have to GRIND many thousands of hours to get all attachments for all guns. Oh wait, you want the vehicle unlocks also??? That'll be another few hundred hours on top of that. Yes, this makes so much sense for a "realistic" battlefield game. Because it's super realistic for soldiers to have to kill thousands of enemies before unlocking a suppressor. This running theme of games requiring thousands of hours invested to unlock all features is absolutely ridiculous and geared towards NEET's and children. Adults with actual lives trying to casually game end up getting the short end of the stick. 

The actual gameplay is "meh" at best. Nothing innovative, nothing interesting, just standard battlefield but watered down a bit. The maps are very average. The BR mode is trash.

I stopped playing battlefield after BF4, came back for BF6 because of all the hype and now I see how atrocious this game actually is. What a waste of time and money. No wonder it lost over 90% of it's player base. I will NEVER buy another Battlefield game ever again and probably will never buy another EA game again either. 

The last REALLY good battlefield game was Battlefield 2 and Bad Company 2. BF3/4 were OK, but nothing like those two. Everything after those has been toilet water.

A 70 dollar game with progression made for a Free to Play game meant to frustrate you so you shell out money to skip the incredibly slow and grindy progression system. It also plays more like Call of Duty than a Battlefield game. SMGs, ARs, and LMGs perform better at range than DMRs not only in ease of use and accuracy but even in damage PER SHOT and time to kill at the same range, automatic weapons are dominant in every situation in general even in the niche cases that some weapons like snipers and shotguns fill, the game has fast and cheap looking animations for everything and there's sliding and slide jumping which negates any penalty you might incur for trying to fire while sprinting, which there kind of isn't any to begin with, you can jump shot people with incredible accuracy, suppression is practically useless, you don't flinch when getting hit, there are attachments that allow you to fire some secondaries while sprinting without stopping, the community in general doesn't play in a team oriented manner due to the kind of community EA has cultivated for this title, all the ranges and mechanics are balanced around short ranges so things work a bit oddly in the new larger maps like zoom levels, slow bullet velocities, the lack of recoil for any of the guns, etc...

This is a minimum viable product with changes and additions being made determined exclusively by a bunch of graphs being misinterpreted by people who probably don't even care about the series as a whole. Shameful.

I wish Battlefield Franchise die and never ever comeback

Every release, like many EA games (looking at you Madden and NCAA) are just rehashes with like 1 or 2 shiny things supposedly added to make it amazing. Every time EA fails.  I have been playing EA stuff since like commodore EA Bird vs. Dr. J and they have become lazy AF for a company that has unlimited resources. How about this EA, make a game like Planetside 2 BUT with current military tech OR close to it and have a perpetual war that NEVER ENDS and your players can pick an allegence to fight for and keep it running day and night. claims.claim: Reviewers report that specific game modes, such as Rush, have been permanently removed after purchase.

citations.review_text: I do not recommend Battlefield 6; it is complete garbage, especially due to the developers' behavior. Our patience as players has officially run out. They did the exact same thing in Battlefield 2042—constantly messing with the game remotely by removing and adding modes. Now they’ve started doing the same here, deleting modes and so on.I contacted EA support since I purchased the game there, but they just made excuses. The chat support claimed they couldn't do anything and rejected my refund request because of my high playtime. This happened even though I cited the EU Digital Content Directive (EU 2019/770), which states that a game and its functions/modes are considered digital content. If the product does not match what was promised in the contract and what the consumer could "reasonably expect" (conformity with the contract), it constitutes a breach of a legally binding agreement.I also cited the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive (2005/29/EC). Advertising specific game modes in marketing materials and on store pages prior to purchase, only to permanently remove them later, constitutes deceptive advertising and misleading practices. Under the Right to Remedy and Refund, if digital content fails to comply or is significantly altered for the worse, the consumer has the right to demand a remedy, an appropriate price reduction, or contract termination (a full refund).And what did EA do? They just replied with their usual nonsense, saying they understand I am upset and asking if it would be okay if they notified me in advance next time they make changes to the game—just absolute rubbish. I kept insisting on a refund, but the chat agent just repeated their script and abruptly left the live chat. I then contacted another agent in a different chat, but that person just repeated the same excuses over and over, hiding behind EA's internal policies.This is the last Battlefield game I will ever buy. It is unacceptable for someone to delete content I paid for. Isn't it tim…
There is a mission to play the gamemode 'Rush'. They removed this gamemode, so you can't get past that mission. That should tell you all you need to know about how much they care about this game.

claims.claim: The anti-cheat software causes kernel-level crashes or blue screen errors on PC.

citations.review_text:
DO NOT BUY - INSTANT BLUE SCREEN / KERNEL CRASHES

I honestly wish I could review the actual game, but I can't even play the product I paid for. Ever since the latest season update, this game has been a literal virus for my system files. If you have a modern high-end Intel rig (like a 14th gen i7), this game will straight up crash your entire PC every 5 to 10 minutes mid-match, throwing constant ntoskrnl.exe Blue Screens.

The community forums are absolutely flooded with people experiencing this exact same loop. It turns out EA pushed a completely broken background update to their trash kernel-level anti-cheat client (Javelin), and it's forcing memory violations that panic Windows into a hard shutdown. 

People are literally wiping their entire operating systems and re-flashing their BIOS just trying to make it past the loading screen, and it still doesn't fix it because the developer's code is fundamentally broken.

EA rolled out a patch today, and guess what? Still blue screening instantly. They updated the game assets but completely ignored the bricked anti-cheat driver that is ruining everyone's PCs. 

The lack of tech support or communication from the community managers is complete garbage. It’s been weeks of total silence while taking people's money for an unplayable, broken build. 

Do not waste your time or risk your hardware's stability on this until they actually fix their anti-cheat. Absolute joke.

***AMD GPU USERS BEWARE*** 

Game was fun on release, unfortunately despite their decades of experience EA somehow manages to write some of the buggiest least reliable AAA games on the market.

When the winter 2025 update released, with it came a bug that made the game unplayable for many people, including myself. Inputting *any* sort of command (move, reload, aim, etc..) would spike the anticheat CPU usage causing the game to stutter for half a second. There was no fix for months, I simply was not able to play the game.

Almost a year after release, today I attempt to launch the game knowing the bug had been resolved, except now whenever I launch the game it corrupts my video card drivers. Factory reinstalling the drivers does not seem to fix the issue. Every time I launch my computer now I get error messages and likely I will now have to spend my entire afternoon deep dive troubleshooting my own hardware because a studio of this "caliber" releases these kinds of vulnerabilities in their product. For all I know, my video card might have just been bricked by this game.

-100/10 this is an embarrassment.

claims.claim: Reviewers note the inclusion of a battle pass and various in-game cosmetic items available for purchase.

citations.review_text: I love Battlefield. It has been one of my favorite game franchises since bad company 2. The gameplay is fantastic, it feels like an actual battlefield game again. I have only two real gripes. One, weapon bloom is disgusting in this game, and feels unnatural. Two, the absolute greed of these people in their microtransactions. Constant battlepass shenanigans that add nothing of any substance or value, and overpriced for what they actually do offer. That said, I can still recommend the game. It's a great time, and I can say that with friends its's ten times as fun.

Look, I just want to be honest with you all. I know it's not the same Battlefield as before, especially after Battlefield 1, 4, or Hardline. Each new game will be different, but I will say this: Battlefield is fun, and I found myself a little addicted to it when I bought it during the summer sales.

If you really love Battlefield and have lost trust in the franchise due to what happened with Battlefield 2042, I understand. However, I promise you the game is enjoyable and works well. I haven’t experienced any significant bugs so far. The maps are decent, and the classes and weapons are fun to use.

Playing with friends in squads enhances the experience because good communication makes the game even better. You don’t necessarily need to be on a call; even random players can often work together effectively. Overall, I find the game enjoyable, and I would highly recommend it to anyone who loves Battlefield but struggles to trust the series after the issues with Battlefield 2042.

One thing to note is that there aren’t any crazy skins like COD. There is a battle pass, but it’s not a big deal; you can enjoy the game without it. There is a battle royale mode, but I personally don’t like battle royale games, I tried it once and didn’t enjoy it much.

I haven’t noticed many negatives, but one thing I will mention is that there aren’t many secondary weapons available. The gadgets are good, but the challenges to unlock items for your classes can be tough. For example, to upgrade the engineer class, you need to use launchers and motion sensors launchers. I forgot the name. The one challenge I really disliked was for the support class, where you have to get 25 assist kills in smoke, which was quite frustrating.

In summary, I think the game is really fun, and I highly recommend giving it a shot. Play for about an hour or two, and if you don’t like it, you can return it. Yes, I know it’s a bit pricey, but you might want to wait for a sale or go ahead and buy it if you’re a fan of…

There is much fatigue going on due to unwanted battle royale upfates, we crave a normal Battlefield. Not industry standard COD copy paste slop. I stopped playing, because at the time, the weapon progression felt sooo slow. Maps kind of way too small, not much vehicular combat, here we go again.
Overpromising and not delivering. Then Game modes being taken out and new added, just to be taken out again.
Not much in the map department either, just FOMO and Skins you can buy in a 70€ game. 
I'm asking myself, why am i doing this ? They have managed to get Vince Zampella on board again and conviced me to give them money... I feel dumb. Those good old times with BF3 and 4 will never come back. ALAS.

They've gotten rid of some of the best game modes that made Battlefield feel like Battlefield in the first place — 
Rush, Squad Deathmatch, and King of the Hill. Instead of building on what made the series great, they keep removing popular modes and changing the formula.

What's even worse is that the official Battlefield website still promotes some of these modes as part of the Battlefield experience, despite them no longer being available in the game. If you're advertising game modes that players can't actually play, that's extremely misleading and, in my opinion, crosses into false advertising territory.

TL;DR: Battlefield still has the foundation to be great, but persistent servers need to return, core modes like Rush/Domination need to return, Conquest needs stronger incentives to play the objective, and REDSEC should stop influencing the balance and direction of traditional multiplayer.

Writing this review on 8/11/2026. I’ve been a Battlefield fan since Bad Company 2, and the series has always had a special place for me because of its mix of CQC and large-scale PvP. That second part is going to be a major complaint further down.

I played the beta and genuinely felt like I was falling in love with Battlefield again after mostly drifting away from the series after BF1. BF2042 was okay, but nothing I’d really rave about. This time around, though, the beta felt great. Yet here we are almost a year later, and somehow the game feels worse despite technically having more “content.” Domination is gone, Rush has been butchered, Breakthrough has been gutted, and some of the changes have reached the point where modes barely feel like what they originally were.

For me, the game is falling short in three major areas.

1. Persistent servers and server browser

This is probably the biggest killer for me. What happened to persistent servers? Is this some kind of ancient lost technology at EA/DICE? Are we seriously still “working our way toward” a proper server browser in 2026?

Any time my friend and I try to play, we either get dropped into a half-empty lobby populated with bots or thrown into a random match that’s already halfway over. It completely kills those longer Battlefield sessions we used to have.

We either sit around waiting roughly 10 minutes for enough real players to fill the server, or we get dumped into a match where our team is already getting demolished so badly that we just back out and try again.

Please bring back persistent servers. Give us official persistent servers, rentable servers, a proper browser, or ideally all three. Battlefield used to make it…

The game has good bones, it definitely had issues at launch but they have been addressed or are being addressed. The recent removal of Rush and KoTH, etc, is a massive blunder. I cant condone removing a long time BF mode. However, the other core modes like conquest are great. The small maps the game launched with will not satisfy core BF players for long, but the new map Tsuru Reef and the Golmud remake are top tier. (I myself no longer run the launch maps) I am excited for carrier assault to come out. The campaign was also fun in my opinion. As they release more properly sized maps and add new weapons / vehicles the game will iron out to be solid.

Bring Rush back, and stop removing modes from my full price shooter 

It is ridiculous that you guys already got rid of the Closed Weapons playlists, despite promising us the option since before launch... now you're removing less populated playlists, and thus gamemodes? 

Stop trying to kill the best Battlefield in years with your terrible decision making
ONLY 4 GAME MODES LEFT TOOK ALL GOOD GAME MODES AWAY NO MORE DOM OR TDM OR STRIKE POINT NEW OWNERS ARE DESTROYING GAME

Not recommended since the recent removal of small game modes. I split my time about 50/50 between the large and small game modes as I enjoy both for different reasons. With the removal of Domination, TDM, and KOTH, they have cut out a large part of the game that I enjoy and I will likely spend a lot less time, if any, on the game going forward.

Why would you take half the game out. rush and domination are integral to BF you are selling what is a solid title for seemingly no reason, the lower tick rate servers are bad enough and a cut corner, to cut game modes in your newest release is wild just shut down 2042 and save the money
undercooked, but a solid title in the franchise

EA/Dice can, will, and already have removed content/modes without warning and for an indefinite amount of time. Rush was the only mode besides casual Breakthrough that I bothered queueing into, and now it's inaccessible through quickplay or custom matchmaking. Apparently the removal of some game modes is to consolidate players in other playlists/modes, which only makes sense to me if you don't care about your product enough to make it actually engaging. The core gameplay is solid, but there isn't anything that really separates BF6 from pretty much any other modern multiplayer shooter you could buy for the same price or cheaper. Please, PLEASE save your time and money for another game that truly deserves it.
DICE just removed multiple core game modes (including rush of all things) for no apparent reason.

-Netcode at its worst point since months
-They keep removing gamemodes like rush and deathmach that have been in the saga since bad company or bf3
-The lack of sense some map and gamode desings:Tsuru Reef,naval focused map,in breaktrough attackers dont have a support vehicle for the first base like in previous games(Ther is an Aamtrac in the campaign btw),not even a small boat
-I want to play this game but it feels dissapointing lately

Classic modes like Rush, Domination, King of the Hill, and Team Deathmatch are being removed (and maaybe rotated back in seemingly at random). 
The reason? Season 4 and still no server browser. 
Instead of letting players find their own matches, they funnel everyone into a handful of playlists to prop up their matchmaking. 
So instead of playing the modes you actually enjoy, you're forced into large-scale Conquest to get farmed by the same Little Bird over and over. 
Removing core Battlefield modes to band-aid broken infrastructure is not a solution!!!

They took away Rush—a Battlefield staple—with absolutely ZERO warning. And somehow, they also removed a cosmetic DLC I PAID FOR as part of the USMC 250th Birthday celebration. No warning. No explanation. No refund.

At this point, it feels like they’re actively stripping away everything that made Battlefield worth playing in the first place. They keep removing features, content, and experiences that players actually enjoyed, while treating the people who spent their money on this game like they don’t matter.

I’ve defended this franchise for a long time, but there’s only so much ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ a player can put up with. You don’t get to take away content people paid for, remove beloved Battlefield staples without warning, and expect players to just keep accepting it.

This is the final straw for me. I’m done.

As 0f 08/01/2026 the developers have started removing large amounts of content from the game. Half the existing game modes and the content and challenges associated with those game modes are entirely gone. No more strike zone. No more Rush. No more King of The Hill. No more Squad Deathmatch or the other small infantry modes. It's all gone.

You paid for it 10 months ago, but it's gone. If I had known, I would've never purchased and just played the FREE TO PLAY GAUNTLET MODES until I got sick of it and then uninstalled and you would not have made a penny off of me. Instead, I happily purchased to play my all time favorite mode, Rush, and now that is gone entirely for "matchmaking health". We had 0 issues finding lobbies for these smaller modes, so I suppose their idea of matchmaking health only applies to Conquest. Oh no, conquest is doing poorly, lets remove ALL THE OTHER CONTENT so they have no choice but to play Conquest. Next thing we know, they'll start removing maps and weapons from the game saying certain maps were removed for matchmaking health as some were not as popular or removing guns because they found that players quit lobbies where they repeatedly died to certain weapons. GTFOH.

TLDR The reason you BOUGHT this game instead of playing the FREE TO PLAY REDSEC/Gauntlet was to play the limited multiplayer content. If you play conquest, fine. But now all that remains is Conquest, Breakthrough, Escalation which is like an off-shoot of Conquest where the map progressively gets smaller, and TDM. If you are a Rush or small infantry modes enjoyer, you just got ripped off.

EDIT
Since people keep commenting the modes are coming back in rotation. Cool, I guess? Still completely unacceptable to just rip the modes like that and now they are supposedly going to be in time based rotations only? Bahahaha. GG. The review stands until these modes are added back in permanently.

The decision to remove Rush is the final straw. Rush has been a core staple of the Battlefield experience for years, yet it feels like it was intentionally set up to fail. By constantly disincentivizing the mode, pushing it into hidden menus, or neglecting its playlist support, player numbers naturally dropped. Using that declining player count as a justification to cut the mode entirely is a self-fulfilling prophecy and a lazy design choice.

To make matters worse, we are still waiting on the promised Server Browser. In previous titles, dedicated communities could easily host and fill 24/7 Rush servers regardless of official playlist rotations. Instead, we were forced to rely on an official matchmaking system that has been an utter disaster since launch due to poor implementation: The constant joining and leaving of bots, the games where one team somehow has 3 players less all through the game and a new player that joins somehow joins the team that already has an numerical advantage.

I'll stop playing for the time being until this mess is addressed. What were you thinking.

DICE, please stop removing game modes and content from Battlefield 6.

Rush - removed
King of the Hill - removed
Squad Deathmatch - removed
Strikepoint - removed
Tactical Obliteration - removed
Operations - removed
Interesting map variants, such as snowy New York and the smokeversion of Contaminated - removed

The game needs more variety, not less. Removing modes and unique map variants makes people who loved to play these modes left the game

Please bring content back to the game and stop treating permanent game modes like temporary playlist rotations, literally decease of modern online games
The removal of several game modes that were advertised since the game was released puts this in the negative for me now. Removed the only mode I regularly came back to.

Normal games: Content and New game modes are added after launch.

Battlefield 6: Just got about 40% of all the gamemodes it had on Release removed.....wtf. 

They even removed Rush?????

Okay first off, i do really like this game. I think it plays very well and i had a lot of fun with my friends.
But i feel the need to give a negative review here because of the latest development and their decision to remove first and foremost Rush and also 3 other gamemodes reasoning they werent played enough... This is something i cant like and i do despite the fact that they thought this was necessary move just to move more players to the "more popular" game modes.
This also makes me very sad since i played the game with a lot of fun for a few houndred of hours.

I will remove this negative review if they decide to revert this change, but as for now im furious and will leave this here as one of my few reviews i have written so far.

The most recent ([b]and silent[/b]) update has removed 15 out of 16 of the maps available for the Rush gamemode.

One of the main factors that got me to buy this game was to play Rush with my friends, to relieve a bit the old days of Battlefield 3 Damavant Peak Rush, the golden era for Battlefield.

And now, as of July 31st 2026, we're forced to play on a [u]SINGLE[/u] map with the Rush gamemode selected, while also removing some other game-modes like Squad Deathmatch and King of the Hill from the search selection [b]completely[/b]. Literally they are forcing you their own playlist rotations.

You basically can't access the maps which came out with the game, for the sake of "matchmaking complains", which is as vague as it can be for the reasoning behind this. If the higher ups at Battlefield Studios aka DICE, keep making these atrocious decisions, you'll lose the remaining playerbase left with this game.

Stop taking one step forward, and then [b]THREE[/b] steps backwards with Battlefield 6. Revert these experimental changes that literaly nobody asked for and focus on improving the game, actually listening to the community, and solving problems that still exist since the beta and are [u]STILL[/u] not adressed.

Until then, this game is for sure Not Recommended, and this comes from someone who used to love this franchise.

Edit 04/08/2026: Rush has been completely removed from matchmaking.

As of writing this review they have recently gutted the custom search for multiplayer, removing half the modes and maps in an effort to improve matchmaking including King of the Hill for some reason. This was done on double weapon xp weekend when the CQB modes have more people playing the grind weapons. Still a great game but this was an exceptionally poor decision in an effort to improve matchmaking. Only downvoting this in an effort to draw attention to reverse or partially reverse this.
Removes half the gamemodes and puts bots in redsec, refuses to elaborate.

I actually enjoyed this game when I played it. My last battlefield was BF4 and my main modes back then were Rush and Conquest. The fact Rush along with a couple other modes were removed is the final straw that broke the camel’s back, and made me uninstall. I’m not gonna be stuck playing a SINGLE mode on a $70 game when it was a staple for me and my friend group since BF3. The fact this game launched at $70 with the state it was in really showed me how bad the AAA space is. (better late than never I guess, genuinely had high hopes for this game, my bad). 

On launch weekend many of us (myself included) experienced and not limited to: constant crashes, being kicked out the party when immediately matchmake the second the game finishes, instability issues at the lowest graphics settings, any version of DLSS causing even more frame drops, terrible netcode/desync/tickrate that somehow rivals COD and I die a meter past the wall (still occurring in S4 with 2GB optic fiber internet BTW), insane controller issues on PC where my character snaps looking up or down at the ground mid gun fight and I’d die from it (I have 3 different controllers and this issue still persists at least once a week), another controller issue to where BF6 hates one of my PS5 controllers to the point I’m soft locked out of my own PC and have to do a hard shut down if CTRL ALT DLT doesn’t work, another controller issue where I cannot access the map at all until I unplug my controller, mouse, and keyboard, this issue specifically I’ve had since launch day, audio issues where everything is so loud except for enemy footsteps, constantly getting backstabbed and flanked by a swat team of sweats running full speed and not a single audio cue, and this is just the tip of the iceberg of the countless issues that haven’t been fixed, and have been persistent since launch. I thought we’d get a break from the usual, but that’s on me fo…

I really loved this game for about the first 4 weeks it was out. The sound design blew me away, it was slower paced and more teamwork-dependent than CoD, the progression felt challenging but rewarding. I was stoked, as it was the first shooter I'd picked up in years. Sure, the fact that I needed to change my secure boot settings was annoying as anything and sure, the UX on all the menus was absolutely awful, but I could forgive these things for the sake of a fun game.

Then, they introduced a battlepass system, began funnelling way too much of dev time / player rewards into a terrible battle royale mode and flooded every inch of every menu with microtransactions and ads for awful looking skins that felt so against the more realistic vibe that the game marketed itself on. All massively insulting considering the massive price this game launched at / continues to be sold at.

Despite this I tried to push on for Season 2, where all we got were two awful maps and a couple of half decent weapons locked DEEP in the battle pass. We saw less of the focus on tweaks and balances that characterised on more on pumping out new slop skins every other weekend for some random holiday or made up occasion.

My friends lost interest, I lost interest and I don't see myself ever going back. It's a shame really; this game had so much potential to be amazing and a mainstay in the rotation, but it just turned into yet another dissappointing Triple-A cash grab.

I've been playing Battlefield since Battlefield 1942 and at 42 years old I've played nearly all of them. This is the most I've enjoyed a Battlefield game since Battlefield 3.

I never really got into Battlefield 4 because at the start it was broken mess and I never returned. Battlefield 1 and Battlefield V just weren't for me—I prefer modern themes which is just a personal preference. As for Battlefield 2042... haha

Battlefield 6 has brought me back. I enjoy the majority of the maps, although until Season 3 they definitely were more focused towards infantry. Even though I'm not as quick as I was in my twenties, I've adapted my playstyle and I'm still having consistently good matches. Very few games keep me wanting to play them every day ten months after launch, but Battlefield 6 is one of them.

My criticisms are fairly minor. The game still crashes occasionally, usually at the start of a round. It only happens every week or two, but it's been an issue since Season 2. The post-launch content also feels a bit sparse. Two new maps per season isn't enough and I'd love to see more weapons added as well. Conquest also feels like it could benefit from more capture points on several maps - they exist on escalation, not sure why they weren't added to Conquest? 

Performance for me has been excellent and my PC is about 6 years old now.

Overall this is easily the best Battlefield in over a decade for me.
